progressCard.title: Your retirement goal
progressCard.growth: Your current {current} grows to {projected} by retirement at a cautious {rate} per year — that's {pct}% of the target shown above (before adding any monthly savings). At the expected {expectedRate} it would be {expectedPct}%.
progressCard.netDebt: Your liabilities exceed your assets by {debt}. Your plan starts from {zero}, so paying down that debt comes on top of the monthly savings we calculate.
progressCard.pensionsCoverAll: Your pension income already covers your expected expenses — no portfolio drawdown required.

savingsCard.title: How much to save each month
savingsCard.pensionsCoverAll: Your pensions cover your expected expenses, so you don't need to save toward a retirement portfolio.
savingsCard.onTrack: Based on your current assets and expected growth, you're on track to reach your goal without saving anything extra. Keep it up!
savingsCard.expectedHint: assumes {rate} / yr — a portfolio that doubles roughly every {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}
savingsCard.indexed: First month's amount, rising with inflation — to {amount} (expected) by retirement.
savingsCard.flat: A flat nominal amount each month until retirement; inflation makes the later payments worth less.
savingsCard.netDebt: These amounts start from {zero} and don't include paying down your current debt.
savingsCard.mortgageNotProjected: Your home mortgage's full balance of {balance} counts as still owed at retirement and is part of your target: add its rate and repayment in the plan to project it.
savingsCard.mortgageOwedAtRetirement: On top of this, your home mortgage repayments of {payment}/mo continue from your income; the {balance} still owed at retirement is part of your target.
savingsCard.mortgageRepaidBefore: On top of this, your home mortgage repayments of {payment}/mo continue from your income until the loan is repaid.

chart.title: Projected portfolio growth
chart.footnote: Four paths: your expected and conservative returns, each shown with your monthly saving plan and with your current portfolio left to grow on its own. The dashed line is your target.

explainer.trigger: Why these numbers? The 4% rule, explained
explainer.rule: The 4% rule is a simple guideline: each year you can withdraw about 4% of your portfolio without running it down over a long retirement. Flip that around and your portfolio needs to be 25× the yearly amount it has to cover.
explainer.customRate: Your plan uses {rate} instead, so your portfolio needs to be {multiple}× that amount.
explainer.marketReturn: ≈ 7–8% long-run expected market return per year
explainer.inflation: − ~2% inflation, so your money keeps its purchasing power
explainer.buffer: − a buffer to stay safe in bad market years
explainer.result: = about 4% you can spend each year
explainer.inflationHandlingRate: Because the withdrawal rate already accounts for inflation during retirement, we don't add inflation twice. Before retirement we grow your expenses and pensions by {rate} a year and grow each part of your portfolio at its own expected return — keeping everything consistent.
explainer.inflationHandling: Because the withdrawal rate already accounts for inflation during retirement, we don't add inflation twice. Before retirement we grow your expenses and pensions by the inflation rate and grow each part of your portfolio at its own expected return — keeping everything consistent.
explainer.simpleTarget: For your plan, using today's expenses and today's pensions (no inflation) the target would be {target}.
explainer.adjustedTargetRate: Adjusted for {years} of {rate} inflation, the realistic target is {target}.
explainer.adjustedTarget: Adjusted for {years} of inflation, the realistic target is {target}.
explainer.difference: {reason, select, fixedPensionsAndMortgage {The difference is inflation, which your fixed pensions don't keep up with, plus the mortgage still owed when you retire.} fixedPensions {The difference is inflation, which your fixed pensions don't keep up with.} mortgage {The difference is inflation, plus the mortgage still owed when you retire.} other {The difference is inflation.}}
explainer.taxExcluded: Both are pre-tax: tax on withdrawals is not included.

introStep.title: Plan your retirement
introStep.body: A few quick questions to turn your retirement goal into a concrete, trackable savings plan — grounded in your real portfolio.

age.title: Pick your retirement age
age.body: Tell us when you'd like to stop working and the lifestyle you want.

pensions.title: Add your pension income
pensions.body: State, company or private pensions cover part of your monthly costs.

number.title: See your number
number.body: We use the 4% rule to compute the portfolio you need — and how much to save each month to get there.

personalStep.title: Your timeline
personalStep.description: When were you born, and when do you want to retire?
personalStep.currentAge: {age, plural, one {You are # year old.} other {You are # years old.}}
personalStep.yearsLeft: You have {years} to build your retirement portfolio.
personalStep.enterBirthDate: Enter your date of birth so we can work out your age.

expensesStep.title: Desired lifestyle
expensesStep.description: The minimum monthly income you'd want in retirement, in today's money.
expensesStep.label: Monthly living expenses (today)
expensesStep.hint: If you own your home, exclude rent — owning it already lowers this number.
expensesStep.future: After {years} of {rate} inflation, that's about {amount} when you retire — the same lifestyle just costs more.

housingStep.title: Your home
housingStep.description: Property is handled differently from investments — let's get it right.
housingStep.ownsHome: I own the home I live in
housingStep.ownsHomeHint: An owner-occupied home isn't counted as retirement funding.
housingStep.homeNotCounted: We don't count your home toward the portfolio that funds retirement — you can't sell it and still live in it. Its real benefit is already reflected in your lower monthly expenses (no rent).
housingStep.mortgageHint: Its balance is not subtracted from your retirement funding: you pay the repayments from your income until retirement, like rent. Any balance still owed when you retire is added to your target.
housingStep.bankBalanceOnly: Your bank reports only the balance. Add the interest rate and monthly repayment to project what is still owed when you retire.
housingStep.withoutTerms: Without both, the full current balance counts as still owed at retirement.
housingStep.equityLabel: Sellable property equity to fund retirement <muted>(optional)</muted>
housingStep.equityHint: For a rental or second property you plan to sell: its value minus any loan on it that isn't tracked in Fiscalis (tracked loans are already subtracted from your net worth). Leave at 0 if none.

pensionsStep.title: Pension income
pensionsStep.description: Monthly income you'll receive in retirement, before touching your portfolio. Enter it in today's money, e.g. the gross amount on your Renteninformation. We take tax and health insurance off gross amounts and adjust indexed pensions for inflation like your expenses.
pensionsStep.deductionLabel: Tax & health insurance on gross pensions
pensionsStep.deductionHint: A flat rate for health & care insurance (≈ 11–12% in the KVdR) plus income tax. The default {rate} turns {gross} gross into about {net} net.

portfolioStep.title: Your portfolio today
portfolioStep.description: This is the starting point we grow toward your target. Choose how each part is expected to grow, or leave out money you won't invest, like an emergency fund.
portfolioStep.noAssets: No assets tracked yet — your plan starts from {zero}.
portfolioStep.netDebt: Your liabilities exceed your assets by {debt}. Your plan starts from {zero} — debt isn't grown at the investment return — so paying it down comes on top of the savings we calculate.
portfolioStep.mortgageWithPayment: The {balance} mortgage on your home is not subtracted here: its {payment} repayments come from your income until retirement.
portfolioStep.mortgage: The {balance} mortgage on your home is not subtracted here: its repayments come from your income until retirement.
portfolioStep.mortgageNotProjected: Without its rate and repayment, the full balance counts as still owed when you retire.
portfolioStep.footnote: Asset values update automatically as your accounts sync, so your progress stays live. Each part grows at its own rate; new savings grow at the scenario return. A home you live in is not included.

assumptionsStep.title: Assumptions
assumptionsStep.description: Sensible defaults are filled in — adjust only if you know what you're doing.

optimisticReturn.label: Expected annual return
optimisticReturn.hint: Long-run market growth. The default {rate} doubles a portfolio every 10 years.

conservativeReturn.label: Conservative annual return
conservativeReturn.hint: A cautious growth assumption for the safer estimate.

inflationRate.label: Inflation rate
inflationRate.hint: How fast prices rise; raises your future expense target.

withdrawalRate.label: Safe withdrawal rate
withdrawalRate.hint: The 4% rule. Lower = safer but needs a bigger portfolio.

assumptionsStep.withdrawalTaxHint: Effective tax on what you withdraw (e.g. capital-gains tax on the gains share). At 0% the target is a pre-tax figure.
assumptionsStep.indexContributionsHint: Off: one flat amount in today's money, worth less every year. On: a lower first amount that grows with inflation.
